energy.note: the 1-minute load average is 2.4, so this machine is not idle, and what follows would be somebody else's work charged to yours. A load average counts RUNNABLE THREADS, so anything above 2 means at least that many are never sleeping. Wait for the machine to go quiet and take the baseline again. Note which way this biases: a contaminated baseline is INFLATED, so idle looks larger than it is, not smaller.

workloads.source: Finite open 2D Ising, the lattice both codebases sample (ferrotherm::ising::grid2d; THRML IsingEBM). 3x3 rather than 4x4 so a few thousand draws can resolve total variation. Not Onsager's infinite lattice, and not a Z1-topology graph.
workloads.oracle: exact enumeration of the Boltzmann distribution

workloads.source: Potts interaction as in Extropic's codon-optimisation note (https://docs.thrml.ai/en/latest/papers/codon-optimization/) and arXiv:2510.23972 Appendix C.1.1, reduced to an enumerable path. ferrotherm::potts heat-bath, index order; THRML one node per block in that order.
workloads.oracle: exact enumeration of the Boltzmann distribution

workloads.source: arXiv:2608.01615 §IV.4 and Appendix J.3, reduced from d=12 to d=8 so a histogram of a few thousand draws can be compared with the exact law. 12 pairs, 10 triples, weights i.i.d. N(0, 0.6^2). The paper does not publish the draw seed; this pin uses ferrotherm::rng::Pcg::new(260801615, 0x54535031), Box-Muller, and rejection-sampled Fisher-Yates. Native chromatic Gibbs of the three-body energy, not Figure 12.
workloads.oracle: exact enumeration of the Boltzmann distribution

workloads.source: Open 4x4 Ising, J=1, beta=0.3. Exact by enumeration (2^16) and by the transfer matrix. Checkerboard blocks are the two-colour Gibbs THRML's Ising quickstart uses (https://docs.thrml.ai/en/latest/).
Open 8x8 Ising, J=1, beta=0.3. exact_energy is the transfer-matrix mean, cross-checked against the Kac-Ward determinant. Checkerboard block Gibbs, as in THRML's Ising quickstart.
Open 16x16 Ising, J=1, beta=0.3. exact_energy is the transfer-matrix mean. A dense 2^32 transfer matrix is not this number. Checkerboard block Gibbs.

Open 32x32 Ising, J=1, beta=0.3. Past the transfer matrix. exact_energy is the mean of a long ferrotherm reference chain on this finite lattice, not Onsager's infinite lattice. Checkerboard block Gibbs.
workloads.oracle: long reference chain on the finite lattice

workloads.source: Open 64x64 Ising, J=1, beta=0.3. Past the transfer matrix. exact_energy is the mean of a long ferrotherm reference chain on this finite lattice, not Onsager's infinite lattice. Checkerboard block Gibbs.
workloads.oracle: long reference chain on the finite lattice

workloads.source: Open 4x4 q=3 Potts, J=1, beta=0.5, below potts::critical_beta. exact_energy is the row transfer matrix. Blocks are the checkerboard, which is THRML's parallel colouring; ferrotherm's Potts heat bath still scans sites in index order.
Open 8x8 q=3 Potts, J=1, beta=0.5. exact_energy is the row transfer matrix (3^8 states per row). Not the codon-optimisation gene, which is not enumerable.
Open 4x4 q=4 Potts, J=1, beta=0.5, below potts::critical_beta(4). exact_energy is the row transfer matrix.
Open 8x8 q=4 Potts, J=1, beta=0.5. exact_energy is the row transfer matrix (4^8 states per row).

arXiv:2608.01615 §IV.4 at the paper's d=12 (4096 states), 18 pairs and 20 triples, N(0, 0.6^2), stream Pcg::new(260801615, 0x54535032). Enumerable. This is the native three-body energy, not Figure 12's compiled kernels. THRML's spin-model notebook is the same polynomial Gibbs conditional on a different graph.
workloads.oracle: exact enumeration of the Boltzmann distribution

workloads.source: Larger three-body model, d=16 (65536 states), 24 pairs and 24 triples, N(0, 0.6^2), stream Pcg::new(260801615, 0x54535033). Enumerable, so the oracle is the Boltzmann mean, not a histogram resolution of every state.
workloads.oracle: exact enumeration of the Boltzmann distribution
